_about: Manual verdicts on the claims the Fact Checker supported, read against the cited passages with the judge's rubric (SUPPORTED: every part stated; PARTIAL: part stated, or a figure, date or scope changed; NOT_SUPPORTED: not stated). Annotated by the AI assistant that built the project (Claude), not by an independent human reviewer.

_notes.eval-baseline-battery-prices C1: The passages present silicon / lithium-metal anodes and new cathodes as next-generation technologies expected to cut costs; the claim turns them into advancements made between 2010 and 2020.
_notes.eval-baseline-heat-pump C1: Heat transfer from outdoor air is stated; 'directly in the room where it is installed' is not.
_notes.eval-baseline-crispr C7: The passage speaks of 'great application prospects' in gene therapy and breeding, not of current use.
_notes.eval-baseline-crispr C8: The passage says applications concern somatic cells and germline editing is debated and illegal in most countries; 'can be used to edit germline cells' overstates it.
_notes.eval-baseline-inflation-france-2022 C1: Production costs are given as a main cause of inflation in France in general; 2022 is not stated in that passage.
_notes.eval-baseline-sea-level-2 C1: Stated verbatim, but off-topic for the sea-level question.
_notes.general: Correct claims are often cited with 3 to 5 passages of which only one or two state them: the Fact Checker over-cites. Several claims end with dangling text ('as highlighted in.', 'ce qui est soutenu par.') left by passage references.
_notes.eval-baseline-nuclear-power-2 C1: High safety standards and unlikely accidents are stated, but under 'issues' (enjeux), not as one of the main advantages; the Swiss passage's 'sécurité d'approvisionnement' is security of supply, not safety.
_notes.eval-baseline-nuclear-power-2 C2/C7: Both stated by the cited passages; rated CONFLICTING by the Fact Checker although no passage contradicts them.
